title: The 60-Second Elevator Ride Up the World's Tallest Building
sources: Khaleej Times, 'Up and down Burj Dubai in intelligent elevators': the double-deck elevators travel at 10 metres per second
Gulf News, 'Special elevator in Burj Khalifa provides top of the world experience': about a minute to the level 124 observation deck
Burj Khalifa: 828 m tall; At the Top, levels 124-125 (about 452 m); Eiffel Tower 330 m. Air pressure from the standard barometric formula (about -5 % at 450 m)
Simulation note: the HUD clock, speed and altitude follow a simple model (5 s doors, 5 s to 10 m/s, cruise, 5 s to stop), not measured data

lines.text: This is the elevator ride to the top of the tallest building on Earth.
Here are the next sixty seconds.
The doors close, and within five seconds you're moving at ten metres a second.
That's thirty-six kilometres an hour, straight up.
About forty seconds in, you pass the height of the Eiffel Tower.
The air pressure drops by about five percent, so your ears pop.
Then it slows, and at about one minute, the doors open on level one hundred and twenty-four.
Four hundred and fifty-two metres up.
Would you look down? Tell me below.
